title: Peace with God: resting in what is finished

passage.why: I do not read your private reading place, so I did not guess today's chapter. Romans 5:1-11 is the plan's own ground for Sabbath rest: peace with God is given, not earned. It works wherever you are in the book this week, and if you have already read it, it is a good second look.

readAloudNote: Left empty on purpose. The ESV wording was not checked this session; read it aloud from the link (Romans 5:1-11).
setting: Paul wrote Romans to the churches in Rome, most likely from Corinth in the mid-50s AD (CONSENSUS). Chapters 1 to 4 argue that all stand guilty and that righteousness comes by faith in Christ. Chapter 5 begins to unpack what that gift does: peace, access, hope and love. It sits at the hinge before chapters 6 to 8 on life in the Spirit.
observe: Mark every use of 'we', 'our' and 'through': who does the action, and who receives it?
Watch the two 'much more' arguments (around verses 9 and 10). What is Paul reasoning from, and to what?
Look at the words Paul uses for us in verses 6 to 10. What does each one say about where we started?

words.note: A verdict word: God's declaration over a sinner who trusts Christ, the heart of the gospel of grace. Whether the word also carries a 'made righteous' sense in Paul is argued between Protestant and Catholic readers. Check the entry in BDAG or at stepbible.org before relying on this note.
words.grade: CONSENSUS on the gospel; DISPUTED on the exact sense (lexicon entry not opened this session)

words.note: In Paul it is relational: the end of hostility with God (compare verse 10, 'enemies'), with the Hebrew shalom in the background. It is not mainly a feeling. Confirm the range in BDAG or HALOT for shalom.
words.grade: CONSENSUS (lexicon entry not opened this session)

words.note: A word from restored relationships: the one who was estranged is brought back. Verses 10 and 11 use it of God and us, and it ties to peace in verse 1. Confirm in BDAG.

crossRefs.note: Jesus himself offers rest to the weary: the same gift from the same Lord.
A Sabbath rest remains for God's people: resting from our own works as God did from his.
Israel's Sabbath is tied to rescue from slavery, not only to creation: rest as remembering what God did.
Where the argument lands: no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.

reflect: What in this passage does God do, and what is left for me to do?
Where do I try to earn standing, with God or with people, that has already been given?
How would today look different if I believed verse 1 as plainly as I believe my own name?

practice.name: Slow meditation on one verse
practice.how: Read Romans 5:1 three times, slowly. Then put it in your own words, one phrase at a time, and pray each phrase back to God. Stay in the verse as long as it holds you; there is no goal to reach.

pray: Adoration: thank God for who he is as the one who makes peace. Confession: name one place you work for what is already given. Thanksgiving: one thing from this week you received, not earned. Supplication: for the week ahead, and for the people at Main Street on Sunday.
journalPrompts: What did I learn about God this week, from the reading or from life?
Where did I notice grace this week, in something I did not earn?
What is one question the week raised that I want to bring to my pastor or Micah, or study next?
